# First model: baseline vs random forest (generated by `python -m src.train`)

Simulated data, rule-made labels (docs/assumptions.md A3). Test set = 20 patients the model has never seen (6724 readings).

| Measure | Baseline (always Normal) | Random forest |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.901 | 0.989 |
| Macro F1 | 0.316 | 0.948 |
| Recall for Critical | 0.000 | 0.899 |
| Precision Normal | 0.901 | 0.997 |
| Recall Normal | 1.000 | 0.995 |
| F1 Normal | 0.948 | 0.996 |
| Precision Warning | 0.000 | 0.913 |
| Recall Warning | 0.000 | 0.940 |
| F1 Warning | 0.000 | 0.926 |
| Precision Critical | 0.000 | 0.944 |
| Recall Critical | 0.000 | 0.899 |
| F1 Critical | 0.000 | 0.921 |

The baseline is right 90% of the time but finds 0% of Critical readings. The forest finds 89.9% of Critical readings in unseen patients (target 90%).

Splitting rows at random instead would report 0.995 accuracy for the forest, against 0.989 on the patient split: too kind, because the model has already met those patients.

Confusion matrices: `docs/results/confusion_matrices.png` and `docs/results/model_comparison.md`.
